title: Coconut-lime fat bombs
summary: Bright, chewy little rounds of shredded coconut, coconut cream and fresh lime, set firm in the fridge.

ingredients.note: the thick part from the top of the can
plus the finely grated zest of 1 lime, if you have it

steps: Put the cup of shredded coconut in a food processor and run it for 1–2 minutes, scraping down once, until it turns fine and slightly oily.
Add the coconut oil, coconut cream, powdered erythritol, lime juice and zest, vanilla and salt and pulse until the mixture holds together when pinched.
Taste and add a little more lime if you like it sharper.
Chill the bowl for 15 minutes if the mixture is too soft to shape, then roll into 14 balls, about 1 tablespoon each.
Roll the balls in the remaining shredded coconut, set them on a lined plate and refrigerate for at least 45 minutes until firm.
tips: These keep a week in the fridge and soften quickly at room temperature, so serve them straight from the cold.

origin.history: This is a modern low-carb recipe rather than a traditional dish. Fat bombs took shape in the 2010s among American ketogenic-diet home cooks, who leaned heavily on coconut because it is high in fat and low in sugar. The coconut-and-lime pairing echoes tropical sweets and drinks, but this form of it is new.
